title: Otanmäki-Humpinsuo OYK:n vaatima vesihuoltokapasiteetin kasvattaminen
description: Otanmäki-Humpinsuo OYK:n vaatima vesihuoltokapasiteetin kasvattaminen Hankinnan kohteena on Otanmäki-Humpinsuo-osayleiskaava-alueen toteutuksen vaatiman vesihuoltokapasiteetin kasvattamisen vaatimien toimenpiteiden suunnittelu. Kajaanin kaupunki on kaavoittanut Otanmäki-Humpinsuo osayleiskaavan ja osana sitä Otanmäki-Alussuo asemakaavaan, jotka mahdollistavat datakeskustoimintojen sijoittamisen alueelle, jonka nykyinen vesihuoltokapasiteetti ei ole riittävä suunnitelluille toiminnoille. Kajaanin Vesi -liikelaitos kilpailuttaa Otanmäki-Humpinsuo osayleiskaavan vaatiman vesihuoltokapasiteetin kasvattamiseen liittyvän vesihuoltosuunnittelukokonaisuuden, joka arvion mukaan sisältää (tarkentuu tarvittaessa suunnittelun edetessä) mm.: -Toimenpidetarpeiden tarkentamisen (ja mitoittamisen) Kajaanin Veden verkostomallilla (Fluidit) -Uuden alavesisäiliö- ja paineenkorottamosuunnittelun kohteen välittömään läheisyyteen -Jätevedenpumppaamosuunnittelua, kohteiden määrä ja laatu tarkennettava verkostomallilla -Olemassa olevan alavesisäiliön ja paineenkorottamoiden putkistomuutosten ja kapasiteetin lisäyksen suunnittelua tarvittavilta osin -Talousvesi- ja jätevesiverkostosuunnittelun tarvittavilta osin -Muutostoimenpiteiden vaatiman ohjausautomatiikan muutossuunnittelun Uudelle kaava-alueelle on alustavasti suunniteltu johdettavan talousvettä Kajaanin taajama-alueelta suunniteltavan syöttöjärjestelyn avulla ja olemassa olevaa yhdysvesijohtoa hyödyntäen nykyinen virtaussuunta kääntäen. Kaava-alueen läheisyyteen sijoitetaan alavesisäiliö ja paineenkorottamo. Tarvittaessa yhdysvesijohdon paineenkorottamoiden kapasiteettia lisätään. Kaava-alueen jätevedet viemäröidään Otanmäen nykyisen asemakaava-alueen ja olemassa olevan siirtoviemärin kautta Kajaanin Peuraniemen jätevedenpuhdistamolle. Viemäröinnin toteuttaminen vaatinee uuden viemärin rakentamista, vanhan saneerausta, jätevesipumppaamoiden rakentamista ja saneerausta sekä tarvittaessa kapasiteetin kasvattamista niin nykyisellä Otanmäen asemakaava-alueella kuin siirtoviemärillä. Kapasiteetin lisäämiseksi tarvittavista toimenpiteistä priorisoidaan ne, jotka ovat välttämättömiä Otanmäki-Alussuo asemakaava-alueen vaatiman vesihuollon kapasiteetin toteuttamiseksi. Nämä toimenpiteet suunnitellaan toteutukseen ja kilpailutukseen asti ja niistä laaditaan tarvittava tarjouspyyntömateriaali. Muu suunnittelu toteutetaan yleissuunnitelmatasolla.,

title: Lobkowiczký palác – modernizace kuchyně a stavební úpravy terasy
description: Předmětem plnění zakázky jsou stavební práce v Lobkowiczkém paláci, které jsou rozděleny na 2 etapy: 1. etapa – zahrnuje modernizaci a rozšíření provozu kuchyně La Favola v 1. PP včetně dodávky gastrotechnologie, 2. etapa – zahrnuje sanaci a rekonstrukci terasy ve 2. NP. V prostoru kuchyně bude provedeno vyklizení a odstranění nevyhovujících povrchů a vybavení, úpravy podlah a kolektoru, nové příčky a předstěny, podhledy, omítky, obklady a podlahy. Součástí jsou rovněž nové rozvody VZT, vody, kanalizace a elektroinstalace, nový rozvaděč a osazení kuchyňské technologie. V prostoru šaten budou provedeny nové příčky, povrchy a související instalace. U terasy bude odstraněna stávající dlažba a část podkladních vrstev, provedena sanace podkladu, nová spádová vrstva, hydroizolační fólie, nové odvodnění včetně měděných chrličů a nová dlažba na terčích. Práce budou prováděny s ohledem na památkovou ochranu objektu a s minimalizací zásahů do historických konstrukcí. Bližší informace k předmětu plnění jsou uvedeny v příloze č. 1 – Projektová dokumentace včetně položkového rozpočtu. Zadavatel poskytuje účastníkům jako přílohu č. 6 Tabulku preferovaných výrobků k dodávce gastrotechnologií, v níž uvádí příklady jednotlivých požadovaných výrobků, výrobce a typy strojů včetně alternativ.

Investiția presupune achiziția a 10 de tramvaie de cca 22 m cu podea complet coborâtă, unidirecționale, dotate cu echipamente ITS, destinate transportului public de călători din municipiul Iași, menite să reînnoiască flota existentă, pentru îmbunătățirea calității serviciului de transport public urban. title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source Technical Support, Administrative Support, and Remote Monitoring Services in Tajikistan
description: THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT. This notice is issued in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) section 5.201 to notify the public of a proposed contract action. The North American Identification Classification System (NAICS) code is 541611 � Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services. The SBA size standard is $24.5 million. The proposed contract action is for Technical and Administrative Services as well as remote monitoring services in Tajikistan. The U.S Agency of Global Media (USAGM) intends to award a contract, on a sole source basis under the authority of FAR 6.302-1, with Nodir Tursun-Zade;THE TERRACES MEYDAN AP S620DUBAI The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 41 U.S.C.3304(a)(1) as implemented by the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 6.302-1, which reads in part, �Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements.� Nodir Tursun-Zade is the only known source able to provide the Technical and Administrative Services, as well as Remote Monitoring Services in Tajikistan. This requirement is for the operation and hosting of the Remote Monitoring System (RMS) located in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, including the Internet connection, for the quality broadcasting and continuous use of the medium wave (MW) and short wave (SW) transmitters in Tajikistan for transmissions of Voice of America (VOA) Dari/Pashto language service to audiences in Afghanistan. Additionally, the vendor must provide part-time technical support for the USAGM broadcasting operations in Tajikistan. USAGM requires these mission-critical services to commence as soon as possible due to an urgent operational need that emerged earlier this month. The U.S. Agency for Global Media's mission is to inform, engage, and connect people around the world in support of freedom and democracy through accurate, objective, and comprehensive news and information. Nodir Tursun-Zade possesses extensive institutional knowledge of USAGM's policies, systems, operational structures, and mission requirements gained through years of direct support to Agency broadcasting activities in Tajikistan. This knowledge, combined with the contractor's unique local presence, technical expertise, and established access to the RMS facility in Dushanbe, enables the immediate provision of services with minimal transition risk. Given the urgent timeframe and the potential disruption to mission-critical broadcasting operations, Nodir Tursun-Zade is the only known source capable of meeting the Government's requirements without interruption to ongoing VOA broadcasts and associated support services. The Period of Performance will be one year from date of award. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. A determination by the Government not to compete this procurement based on responses to this notice is solely at the discretion of the Government. Interested parties who believe they possess the capability to satisfy this requirement should submit documentation that clearly demonstrates their capability. Responses to this notice shall be received no later than September 24, 2026 at 8:00AM EST. All responses must be in writing only via email to the point of contacts specified in this notice. Telephone requests or inquires will not be accepted. Any cost associated with the preparation and submission of data or information in response to this notice is the sole responsibility of the respondent and will not be reimbursed by the Government.

title: EEA/CCE/TC/26/010 - Topic Centre on Climate Risk and Resilience: Knowledge Development
description: To drive progress towards a climate resilience Europe, the EEA will continue providing essential data, information and policy-relevant insights that inform the design and implementation of adaptation measures, risk management strategies and societal preparedness efforts. A key priority is to track and assess progress on EU's climate resilience. Knowledge exchange will support EU Member States in preparing national climate risk assessments and adaptation policies. The EEA will also play a role in the implementation of potential outcomes for the foreseen European Integrated Framework for Climate Resilience. With a focus on resilience indicators, sectoral progress and broader economic and societal resilience, the EEA aims to develop relevant and actionable knowledge products for Europe. The focus of this new Topic Centre will be predominantly on the knowledge and networking services. However, tasks under these services will also cover some data services and will build on work conducted under the Topic Centre on Climate and Resilience: Reporting, Tools and Online Knowledge support. As such, collaboration is expected between the two Topic Centres.

Anskaffelsen omfatter lovpålagte og øvrige bedriftshelsetjenester, herunder bistand innen systematisk HMS-arbeid, sykefraværsoppfølging, arbeidsmiljøkartlegging, helseundersøkelser, kurs og rådgivning. Leverandøren skal tilby en tverrfaglig bedriftshelsetjeneste med tilgang til relevante fagressurser og en digital løsning for bestilling, rapportering og statistikk. Det skal inngås rammeavtale med én leverandør for Bodø kommune. Avtalen har en varighet på 4 år med opsjon på ytterligere 2 år.

title: MESO QuickPlex SQ Plate Reader
description: FAR 6.302-1 � Only One Responsible Source Solicitation Number 75N98026Q01214 Title MESO QuickPlex SQ Plate Reader Description of Requirement The National Institutes of Health intends to award a contract to Meso Scale Discovery on a sole-source basis pursuant to FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements, for the acquisition of a MESO QuickPlex� SQ 120MM. The MESO QuickPlex� SQ 120MM Pursuant to FAR 6.302-1, the Government intends to solicit and award a Purchase Order on a sole-source basis because the Government's minimum technical requirements can only be satisfied by the Meso Scale Discovery. The MESO� SECTOR S 600MM, MESO QuickPlex� SQ 120MM, and MESO QuickPlex Q 60MM laboratory analytical instruments are manufactured and sold solely by Meso Scale Discovery (MSD), a division of Meso Scale Diagnostics, LLC. of Rockville, MD. The imagers are compatible only with microwell plates and immunoassay kits sold by MSD and vice versa. MSD utilizes electrochemiluminescence to detect binding events on patterned arrays. There are no other technologies that enable multiplexed measurement using electrochemiluminescence for detection. And there are no other suppliers that provide an electrochemiluminescence detection system that is not reliant on beads or flow cells. The MSD� assay platform is unique in its method for detection as outlined below: � Electrochemiluminescence (ECL) Detection � MSD�s ECL detection utilizes proprietary SULFO-TAG� labels that emit light upon electrochemical stimulation initiated at the electrode surfaces of MULTI-ARRAY� and MULTI-SPOT� microplates through biomolecular interactions between the analyte and labeled reporter at the surface. � Sample Throughput � The SECTOR� S 600MM instrument can read plates in 1 to 1.5 minutes regardless of the multiplexing level. As an illustrative example, the S 600MM instrument can read approximately 50 96-well, 10-spot plates (measuring 10 analytes per each well) per hour resulting in 48,000 measurement per hour. � Non-fluidic, high-reliability instruments � All assay processing and readout steps take place in MSD�s disposable plate-based format. No sample is transferred from the plate to the instrument and hence there are no complicated fluidics that may be prone to clogging and other failures. MSD�s instrumentation has been highly praised by customers for exceptional reliability. The HBGS requires a sensitive, high-throughput analytical platform to support biochemical profiling, multiplex biomarker measurement, and experimental validation relevant to rare biochemical diseases. This activity is directly tied to the Clinical Research activities in the Human Biochemical and Genetics Section (HBGS), which conducts active, protocol?driven patient?based investigations, consistent with NIH definitions of clinical research. The MESO QuickPlex SQ 120MM provides the capabilities necessary for these applications through MSD�s proprietary electrochemiluminescence (ECL) technology, which is only available from Meso Scale Discovery and not offered by any other vendor. The instrument enables rapid multiplex analysis, reading up to 50 plates per hour with high sensitivity and reliability, which is critical for processing diverse patient-derived samples and supporting both research and diagnostics in the Section. The continuation of this project will continue to simulate a clinical trial with our pulmonary fibrosis patients. Accordingly, the Government intends to award a sole-source contract to Meso Scale Discovery, Inc. pursuant to FAR 6.302-1. This notice is not a request for competitive quotations. However, interested parties that believe they can meet the Government's requirements may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to provide the required supplies and meet all specified technical and operational requirements. The Government will consider all timely capability statements received and determine whether the acquisition should proceed as a sole-source procurement or be competed. The Government anticipates making an award approximately five (5) calendar days after the closing date of this notice, unless the Government determines that another responsible source is capable of meeting the requirement. Capability statements shall be submitted electronically to davisroshonna@mail.nih.gov no later than 9:00 a.m. EDT on September 24, 2026. Please reference Notice No. 75N98026Q01214 in the subject line of the response.

title: Whole genome sequencing for investigation of age-related chronic disease in HANDLS participants
description: Investigators in the Healthy Aging in Neighborhoods of Diversity across the Life Span (HANDLS) study require whole genome sequencing (WGS) processing to expand our current research examining whether genetic variants contribute to age-related chronic diseases. Samples from HANDLS participants have been collected over 20 years and many are over 10 years old. A contract is required because the Government does not have available facilities or resources to perform this work consistent with other WGS performed on other HANDLS samples. The objective of this work is expanding our current research to examine health differences associated with age-related chronic diseases through whole genome sequencing to investigate the contributions of genomics to the burden of disease incidence, prevalence, morbidity, and mortality in populations within the United States. The long-term goal is to create a consistent dataset of whole genome sequencing to complement the longitudinal HANDLS behavior and health data. The contractor will deliver plates to the Government sufficient to run 600 samples, some of which have been stored for ten or more years. The contractor will perform whole genome sequencing, and specifically shall: Sequence libraries on the NovaSeq X-Plus platform with 25B-300 flow cells using 150 bp paired end runs and NovaSeq workflow-series 10B sequencing run confirm genomic DNA quantity and quality by performing DNA concentration measurements and volume checks Re-attempt sequencing in the case that DNA quality and quantity is sufficient, but sample fails sequencing-based quality control Examine agarose gels on all samples as an industry-standard method for screening DNA marker quality prepare PCR-free sequence libraries for all samples Sequence the libraries at a minimum of 30x coverage with 2�150 base pair runs Perform primary and secondary analysis of the sequencing data including but not limited to read alignment, variant calling, and quality control analyses Quality control checks will include confirming sex, identifying unexpected duplicates and relatedness, confirming relatedness, providing sample performance information and sample identity confirmation against the sequencing data, in addition to confirming coverage, contamination, mapped reads, and other general quality metrics. Alignment and variant calling will be performed with the DRAGEN Germline pipeline. After quality is confirmed, joint variant calling should be performed producing a multi-sample VCF file. Provide written summaries and documentation of the methods used to perform the whole genome sequencing pipeline Supply the whole genome sequencing data in a mutually acceptable electronic format that preserves study participants� confidentiality. Data delivered will include: per sample CRAMs per sample gVCFs per sample VCFs joint-called multi-sample VCF per sample structural variant and CNV calls QC report and data dictionary Sample manifest with flagged problems Following data delivery and upon request by the Government, the contractor shall provide attendance at Government laboratory staff meetings, and the contractor shall provide technical consultations as needed. The contractor will also ship overnight on dry ice any leftover samples on plates to the Biomedical Research Center in Baltimore, MD. Please refer to the attachments for complete details, specifications and relevant information.

description: ****AMENDMENT 003 - An attachment has been added. The document contains questions and answers related to the Challenge. **AMENDMENT 002 - An attachment has been added. The document contains questions and answers related to the Challenge. *Please note that the ISC website will be available on August 13, 2026 at 10:30am EST.* This Challenge Notice is issued under the Innovative Solutions Canada Program (ISC) Call for Proposals 004 (EN578-24ISC4). For general ISC information, Offerors can visit the ISC website at: http://www.ic.gc.ca/eic/site/101.nsf/eng/home Please refer to the Solicitation Documents Innovative Solutions Canada Program Call for Proposals – 004 - Tender Notice | CanadaBuys https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/cb-331-17030872 which contains the process for submitting a proposal. Here are a few things you need to know before you get started on your application to this challenge: 1. This challenge is only open to receive proposals for Phase 2 (prototype development) of our Challenge Stream. - Proposed solutions that fall within technology readiness level (TRL) 5 and 9 can be submitted to this challenge: https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en/isc-technology-readiness-level-scale 2. We recently made changes to the Challenge Stream; we have outlined the new parameters: https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en/challenges Steps to apply: Step 1: Read this challenge. Step 2: Read the Call for Proposals : https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/cb-331-17030872 Step 3: Propose your solution here : https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en/minerva-initiative-arctic-uncrewed-air-system?auHash=6CHvUJo1TFseah1BoKfUzu0d5rKaz3SNEPiCsitv82I MINERVA Initiative – Arctic Uncrewed Air System The Department of National Defence (DND) and the Canadian Army (CA) requires an uncrewed aircraft system (UAS) to conduct intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance in Arctic operational conditions that is domestically produced, easy to operate and maintain, and adequately rugged to enable the Canadian soldier to successfully fight and survive on the future battlefield. Challenge sponsor: Department of National Defense (DND) Funding mechanism: Contract Opening date: August 13, 2026 Closing date: September 24, 2026, 14:00 Eastern time Challenge Problem statement The Canadian Army (CA) soldier is facing an increasingly complex and dangerous battlespace in the future. A major element of the complexity and danger is the extreme cold weather conditions inherent in operations in the Arctic environment as the CA and Canadian Ranger (CR) executes responsibilities for sovereignty operations and Search and Rescue (SAR). The CA presently lacks an UAS capable of conducting intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance in Arctic conditions. The CA requires an innovative uncrewed aircraft system (UAS) that provides an uncrewed alternative to gather information shareable with Other Government Departments (OGD) while operating in extreme cold weather conditions. This innovation must be simple, durable, and highly survivable providing soldiers with an effective capability for future conflicts that integrates seamlessly into operations while minimizing training and maintenance requirements, allowing soldiers to focus on their mission. Desired outcomes and considerations Essential (mandatory) outcomes The proposed solution must: 1. Be composed of an: a. Air vehicle: The airframe containing the onboard electronics, propulsion, and payload. b. Sensor payload: The equipment required for navigation and to complete a mission, such as cameras or imaging systems. c. Ground control station: The system (laptop, tablet, or handheld controller) used by the human operator to control flight and manage missions. d. Radio: The wireless system that connects the GCS to the UAS to transmit commands and receive telemetry/data. e. Battery with charger: A battery for the UAS and a battery charger capable of charging multiple batteries simultaneously. f. Remote antenna: An external antenna placed 30m away from the GCS to enhance signal strength, reduce interference, and extend operational range. 2. Operate in various weather conditions. At a minimum: a. Operate in a temperature range of -40°C and +40°C; b. Operate in a minimum windspeed of up to 55 km/hr; c. Operate in light rain or snow ranging from 0.5mm/m²/hr; and d. Operate in moderate icing conditions ranging from 6 g/cm²/hr. 3. Have both a minimum operational radius of 20km and a minimum endurance of 90 min. in continuous movement. 4. Have a sensor that enables the operator to recognize¹ a target at a minimum distance under the following conditions: a. Day: Person (180cm) at 0.5km, Vehicle (5m x 3m x 2m) at 1km b. Night: Person (180cm) at 0.25km, Vehicle (5m x 3m x2m) at 0.5km 5. Be stowable in a 240-litre container. 6. Have a maximum takeoff weight of no more than 25kg. 7. Be capable of operating at a minimum operational altitude of 1000 feet Above Ground Levels (AGL). 8. Allow for operability of the GCS while wearing winter gloves. ¹. “Recognize” is defined by the Johnson Criteria: Detection, Recognition, and Identification (DRI) are all guidelines that have been set in place by The Night Vision Thermal Imaging Systems Performance Model, also referred to as the Johnson criteria (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnson%27s_criteria). Additional Outcomes The proposed solution should: 1. Be deployable from a stowed state to ready state in 30 minutes or less. This includes completing all tasks (i.e. unloading vehicle, loading/fueling the power system and loading/configuring mission set) such that the vehicle is fully prepped and ready for launch. 2. Be capable of conducting vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) in a maximum area of 2 m². 3. Emit no more than 5 decibels Sound Pressure Level (dB SPL) of noise in all frequency ranges, measured at a 500m distance from the UAS. 4. Be capable of operating with fibre-optic wire, or an alternate non-Electromagnetic (EM) spectrum means. 5. Return to a pre-determined location, hover/loiter, and/or climb in case of loss of link. 6. Have an aggregated projected production cost of $60,000 CAD or less per system. 7. Have a Ground Control Station (GCS) that: a. Incorporates a training simulation capability for Mission Planning. b. Has a minimum remote antenna cable length of 50m. c. Enables UAS navigation via both direct operator control and autonomously using waypoint navigation via the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS). d. Displays the following information: i. Location of vehicle in 6 figure Military Grid Reference System (MGRS); ii. Orientation of vehicle (pitch/roll/yaw); iii. Point of aim of camera in 6 figure MGRS; iv. Real-time full motion video feed; v. Altitude in Metres above Sea Level (MSL); and vi. Battery life. e. Can interface with the Tactical Assault Kit (TAK) battle management system to push UAS Position Location Information (PLI) and target PLI. 8. Have an alternate non-electric or hybrid power system that does not rely solely on a battery (i.e. a gas-powered system or a gas/electric hybrid power system). 9. Demonstrate capacity in having its critical components produced and sourced in countries within the NATO alliance, NATO Partners or Major Non-NATO Allies (https://www.nato.int/en/what-we-do/partnerships-and-cooperation/natos-partnerships) . To achieve this, Offerors are requested to provide as an attachment to their proposal, a list identifying the solution's critical components, the country of production and sourcing for each component. Critical components and requested information for each Critical components are defined in the table below: Critical Components 1. Radio 2. Ground control station (GCS) 3.On-board computer 4. Any software Requested

title: X-Ray Inspection System
description: Introduction The National Research Council of Canada (NRC) is seeking information regarding advanced X-ray inspection systems to support the research, development, characterization, and failure analysis of rechargeable battery technologies. The NRC's Automotive and Surface Transportation (AST) Research Centre conducts research and testing on a broad range of energy storage systems, including lithium-ion, sodium-ion, solid-state, and emerging battery technologies intended for transportation, aerospace, defence, and stationary energy storage applications. As battery systems become increasingly complex and energy dense, there is a growing need for non-destructive techniques capable of revealing internal structural features and defects that may affect performance, reliability, safety, and manufacturability. X-ray inspection provides a valuable method for visualizing internal battery structures without disassembly, enabling researchers to evaluate cell construction, manufacturing quality, degradation mechanisms, and failure modes throughout the product lifecycle. The AST team operates one of Canada's leading battery testing and characterization facilities, supporting government, industry, and academic partners across the battery value chain. The addition of advanced X-ray inspection capabilities would complement existing electrochemical, thermal, and safety testing infrastructure by providing high-fidelity internal imaging of battery components and assemblies. Objectives The primary objective of this Request for Information (RFI) is to identify and evaluate commercially available X-ray inspection systems suitable for rechargeable battery research, development, characterization, and failure analysis applications. NRC is particularly interested in high-resolution two-dimensional (2D) X-ray imaging systems capable of examining battery cells, cell components, and related assemblies. While inspection throughput is not a primary consideration, image quality, spatial resolution, defect detection capability, sample manipulation flexibility, system versatility, and suitability for laboratory-based research are of significant interest. The information gathered through this RFI will assist NRC in understanding the current state of available technologies, identifying relevant capabilities and limitations, and informing the development of future technical requirements.the objectives of the request for information

title: Freedom Connection Natural Gas Pipeline
description: SOURCES SOUGHT - REQUEST FOR INFORMATION FREEDOM CONNECTION NATURAL GAS PIPELINE THIS NOTICE IS FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP) OR INVITATION FOR BID. This announcement seeks information from industry which will be used for preliminary planning purposes. This is not a solicitation for proposals, and no contract will be awarded from this synopsis. No solicitation, specifications or drawings are available at this time. 1.0 Introduction and Purpose The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Latin America and Caribbean District (SAA) is conducting market research for the construction of the Freedom Connection Natural Gas Pipeline in Puerto Rico. The results of this market research will help determine the final procurement strategy. USACE-SAA is issuing this follow up Request for Information due to changes in the design, scope of work and acquisition strategy. This request is to gain knowledge of interest, capabilities, and qualifications of Small Business concerns, certified HUBZone, 8(a), Woman-Owned Small Businesses, Economically Disadvantaged Woman-Owned Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Business or Veteran-Owned Small Business. The responses or submissions will be used for informational and planning purposes only and do not constitute a commitment by the Government. The Government will not pay for any information submitted, and respondents will not be notified of the results. Submission or responses to this request for information is not a prerequisite for any potential future offerings. 2.0 Background The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) is funding the Freedom Connection Project. The objective is to enhance the resilience of Puerto Rico�s northern power grid by improving fuel infrastructure. This project involves constructing an approximately 4.2-mile, 20-inch diameter natural gas pipeline to supply the Palo Seco Power Plant from the existing San Juan liquid natural gas (LNG) terminal. SAA anticipates soliciting and awarding one (1) design-bid-build solicitation in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Parts 15 and 36. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 237120 - Oil and Gas Pipeline and Related Structures Construction. The small business size standard for this NAICS code is US $45 million. The estimated magnitude of construction is between $25,000,000 and $100,000,000. Anticipated award date is in the second quarter of Fiscal Year 2027. Performance Period is 365 calendar days from NTP. 3.0 Scope of Work The scope of work includes all integrated procurement, labor, equipment, and services required to construct and commission the new pipeline based on a forthcoming final engineering design. Core responsibilities include: � Materials Procurement: Procure all necessary items, including long-lead items such as 20� steel pipe, valves, fittings, and instrumentation, ensuring compliance with the final design and industry standards. � Site Work: Prepare access roads and rights-of-way, and perform site clearing, grading, and stabilization. � Pipeline Installation: Execute all installation activities, including: Trenchless methods (e.g., Horizontal Directional Drilling - HDD). Open trench cut-and-cover installation. Pre-fabrication of materials. Pipeline welding, non-destructive testing (NDT), and inspection. Application of protective external coatings. Above-grade pipeline installation, potentially requiring more than 50 feet deep concrete piles. � Facilities Construction: Build all standalone facilities, including mainline block-valve stations and pig launcher/receiver stations, including electrical and instrumentation. � Delegated Design: Manage and execute any potentially delegated design elements (e.g., temporary works, trench shoring, specialized HDD drill profiles, or structural supports), including coordination with and sealing by licensed Professional Engineers. � Testing and Commissioning: Perform hydrostatic pressure testing, leak detection, and all pre-startup commissioning protocols. � Restoration and Handover: Restore all disturbed areas and formally transfer the completed pipeline and facilities to the owner/operator. 4.0 Requested Information for Capability Statement Interested firms must submit a capability statement (limited to 10 pages) that addresses the following. Responses should be tailored to demonstrate the firm's ability to successfully manage and execute this integrated procurement and construction project. Corporate Information & Experience 1. Company Profile: Provide your firm's name, address, point of contact (POC), CAGE Code, and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). 2. Business Category: Specify your firm's socioeconomic status (e.g., Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), HUBZone, 8(a), Woman-Owned Small Business). 3. Bonding Capacity: Include documentation from your bonding company showing current single and aggregate performance and payment bond limits. 4. Project Experience: Interested construction firms may provide no more than three (3) example projects where the interested firm served as the prime contractor. Each project must include the name, title, project role, e-mail address, and telephone number of at least one reference. References may be used to verify project size, scope, dollar value, percentages and quality of performance. Example projects must be of similar size and scope. Projects similar in scope to this project include: Natural gas pipeline project of similar magnitude and complexity where your firm was responsible for both materials� procurement and construction. Civil projects involving trenchless technologies like HDD, and work in dense urban or environmentally sensitive areas. Each project must comprise of detailed scope of the work, performance timeline, dollar value, customer name. Construction of pipelines of more than 1 mile in length including trenchless pipeline installation, including horizontal directional drilling, jack and bore, and other trenchless technologies. 5.0 Submission Instructions � Deadline: Responses must be submitted via email no later than 10:00 AM (AST), Tuesday, 24 September 2026. � Email To: Angel.J.Martinez@usace.army.mil and Meranda.R.Booth@usace.army.mil. � Format: No hardcopy or facsimile submissions will be accepted. title: Pre-Solicitation Notice of Intent to Sole-Source
description: PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE TO NEGOTIATE ON A SOLE SOURCE BASIS The Office of Acquisition and Agreements Management (OAAM), Acquisition Management Division (AMD), of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), on behalf of the NIST Material Measurement Laboratory (MML), intends to negotiate on a sole source basis with Grenova, Inc. (formerly Peak Analysis and Automation, Inc.), 1900 Ellen Road, Richmond, VA 23230-4213 (UEI: XSCGMEZKBZB9), for the acquisition of a new Living Measurement Systems Foundry (LMSF) automation system and equipment necessary to modernize the existing Government-owned LMSF automation system. NIST requires a complete, integrated laboratory automation solution to expand the capabilities of the existing LMSF. The Contractor shall furnish one new LMSF automation system capable of supporting automated microbial culture, sample preparation, and analytical workflows. The system shall include all required laboratory instrumentation, robotic liquid handling equipment, robotics, automated plate handling and storage equipment, biological containment equipment, computers, software, firmware, licenses, accessories, and other components necessary to provide a complete and fully operational automation system. The Contractor shall also furnish a new Hamilton Company MicroLab STAR liquid handling platform and all associated hardware, software, firmware, licenses, and integration components necessary to modernize the existing Government-owned LMSF. The replacement platform shall be integrated with the remaining Government-owned equipment while preserving the existing system's automation functionality, software operation, laboratory workflows, operating parameters, and measurement methodologies. As part of furnishing the new and modernized LMSF automation systems, the Contractor shall provide all necessary system design, configuration, integration, programming, Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), delivery, installation, Site Acceptance Testing (SAT), commissioning, documentation, operator training, and warranty support necessary to provide NIST with complete and operational systems. The anticipated acquisition will be Firm-Fixed-Price and will consist of an eighteen (18)-month base period for delivery, integration, installation, testing, training, and acceptance of the new and modernized LMSF automation systems. The acquisition is also anticipated to include three (3) one-year option periods for maintenance and support following expiration of the applicable warranty periods. Sole source determination is based on the following: NIST's minimum requirement is not simply for commercially available laboratory instrumentation. The Government requires a second LMSF automation system that functions as a measurement-equivalent and interoperable automation platform with the existing LMSF. The new and modernized systems must preserve compatibility with existing laboratory workflows, automation routines, software functionality, operating parameters, and measurement methodologies. Grenova, Inc. (formerly Peak Analysis and Automation, Inc.) designed, integrated, delivered, installed, and commissioned the Government's existing LMSF automation system and has subsequently provided maintenance, technical support, and system upgrades. As the original system integrator, Grenova possesses unique knowledge of the existing LMSF system architecture, hardware and software integration, automation programming, equipment interfaces, control strategies, and operational characteristics. NIST has operated and characterized the existing LMSF for approximately eight years. During this period, NIST has quantified contributions to measurement uncertainty associated with robotic manipulation, liquid transfers, incubation, spectrophotometric measurements, and other automated operations. The Government therefore requires the second system to reproduce the operational characteristics of the existing LMSF sufficiently to permit the two systems to function as interchangeable measurement systems without introducing unacceptable differences in measurement performance. The modernization of the existing LMSF requires replacement of the currently integrated Hamilton MicroLab STAR liquid handling platform while maintaining the functionality of the remaining Government-owned automation system. Successful modernization requires integration of the replacement equipment with existing robotics and instrumentation and migration or preservation of applicable automation software, configuration files, control logic, drivers, communication settings, automation routines, and operational parameters. The original LMSF was acquired under Contract No. SB134118SU0017. The original contract did not include FAR clause 52.227-14 or otherwise establish Government rights to use technical data, including designs developed under the award. Consequently, it is unclear to what extent the Government may use the original system's hardware and software designs, integration information, automation routines, and related technical information to enable another source to reproduce the existing LMSF design. Market research indicates that Grenova is the only known source capable of furnishing the complete requirement, including a functionally equivalent LMSF automation system, the equipment and integration necessary to modernize the existing Government-owned LMSF, and follow-on support for both systems. Acquisition from another source is expected to result in substantial duplication of cost and unacceptable delays associated with redevelopment, integration, testing, requalification, and validation of an alternative system. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 334516 � Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing, with a small business size standard of 1,000 employees. No solicitation package will be issued. This Notice of Intent is not a request for competitive quotations; however, responsible sources that believe they can satisfy the Government's requirements may submit a written capability statement demonstrating their ability to furnish the complete requirement. Capability statements shall specifically address the respondent's ability to: Furnish a complete laboratory automation system incorporating robotic liquid handling equipment, laboratory instrumentation, robotics, automated plate handling, automation software, and biological containment equipment; Furnish and integrate equipment manufactured by multiple Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) into a unified laboratory automation system; Furnish a system capable of operating interoperably with the Government's existing LMSF while preserving or reproducing existing automation routines, software functionality, operating parameters, laboratory workflows, and measurement methodologies; Furnish and integrate a replacement Hamilton Company MicroLab STAR liquid handling platform into the existing Government-owned LMSF while preserving the functionality and performance of the remaining system; and Provide the warranty, maintenance, replacement parts, software support, and technical support necessary to sustain both LMSF automation systems. Respondents shall identify any Government-furnished technical data, system design information, software, interface documentation, proprietary information, licenses, or other information that would be required for the respondent to furnish a system satisfying the Government's requirements. Responses must be received by September 24, 2026. A determination by the Government not to compete the proposed acquisition based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement.

title: MSD Infrastructure Repairs Phase 2
description: The U. S. Army Corps of Engineers, St. Louis District proposes to provide Federal construction assistance to Metropolitan St. Louis Sewer District for the rehabilitation of combined sewers. The subject project consists of sewer rehabilitation utilizing Cured-In-Place Pipe (CIPP) methods. The rehabilitation work is generally described within of the Metropolitan St. Louis Sewer District specifications as follows: The work will consist of furnishing all labor, equipment, operators, supervision, supplies and materials, and incidentals necessary to perform sewer rehabilitation of approximately 2,675 lineal feet of sewers, sized at 21 inches in diameter to 24 inches in diameter utilizing CIPP methods. The project is within the MSD Boundaries, which includes the City of St. Louis and St. Louis County, Missouri. The work will be performed in various quantities at various sites. The initial work identified is in MSDs Service Area 1. Refer to W912P926BA008 for Pre-Solicitation Notice.

title: TECOM Range and Training Area Management (RTAM) Support Services M00264-26-R-0005
description: The Marine Corps Installation, National Capital Region, Regional Contracting Office (MCINCR-RCO), Marine Corps Base Quantico, VA currently has a follow-on requirement for the United States Marine Corps (USMC), Training and Education Command (TECOM) Range Training Area Management (RTAM) Support. The procurement of services in support of TECOM shall be solicited as a competitive Small Business concern. The contemplated contract will be a single award, Firm Fixed Priced contract. The resultant contract will have a 12?month base period followed by four (4) additional 12?month option periods, which may be exercised at the Government�s discretion. The NAICS code associated with this requirement is 541990. This action will be solicited utilizing FAR Part 12 in conjunction with Part 15 Contracting by Negotiation procedures. All terms, conditions, evaluation procedures, and instructions to offerors will be specified in an upcoming Request for Proposals (RFP) that will be posted on this website (SAM.gov). The proposed solicitation number for this action is M00264-26-R-0005. All responsible sources must submit a proposal to be considered for this requirement. All interested parties must be registered in the System Award Management (SAM.gov). It is the responsibility of the interested parties to independently review the referenced web link (SAM.gov) frequently for updates to any and all documents. Potential offerors will be responsible for downloading their copy of the RFP and amendments, if any. SCOPE OF WORK: The Range and Training Area Management Branch, TECOM requires contractor support to provide specialized expertise for the Marine Corps Range Program, including aviation range safety, ground range safety, laser range safety, range certification, Range Facility Management Support System (RFMSS) support, administrative services, range safety training, Range Managers Tool Kit (RMTK) support, Geographic Information Systems (GIS) data maintenance and development, Range Operations Professional Development (ROPD) curriculum development, range training systems, and installation?level range operations support. These services require multi?service experience in classroom instruction, range integration, range certification, and airspace/Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) workflows. This support is essential to the modernization, upgrading, transformation, safety, and sustainment of USMC Operational Training Ranges.

CFC 273.0 PORTES ET MENUISERIE EN BOIS - Transformation et agrandissement d'un ESE à Yverdon-les-Bains - K2
description:
La Fondation St-George, établissement socio-éducatif fondé dans les années 1980 à Yverdon-les-Bains, accueille actuellement 68 résidents en internat et 11 en externat. Dans le cadre de son développement, elle lance un projet d’extension pour ajouter 11 places en internat et 3 en centre de jour, tout en modernisant ses infrastructures existantes.


Le site, réparti sur les parcelles 3303 (Yverdon-les-Bains) et 459 (Montagny-près-Yverdon), comprend un patrimoine bâti historique et plusieurs bâtiments fonctionnels. Le projet prévoit la construction de deux nouvelles structures d’hébergement (Tamaya et Situation Complexe), ainsi que de deux bâtiments de services (Fermette et Cafétéria), tout en restructurant les espaces administratifs et techniques. Les bâtiments actuels Tamaya et Fermette seront démolis pour laisser place aux nouvelles constructions, intégrées harmonieusement dans le tissu existant.

title: Sources Sought/Market Intelligence Notice: Selfridge KC-46 Dual Bay Hangar Complex � Use of Construction Management at Risk using Other Transaction Authority (OTA)
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / MARKET INTELLIGENCE NOTICE This is a Request for Information (RFI) for market intelligence and for informational purposes only. This announcement does not constitute a Solicitation or a Request for Proposal (RFP), and no solicitation is currently available. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. The Government will not be obligated to award any agreement or contract because of this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the preparation or submission of information. Submitting a response will not affect a firm�s ability to submit a proposal should formal solicitation be issued in the future. NAICS Code: 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction (Note: While Other Transaction Authority is not subject to FAR-based small business regulations, this NAICS code is provided for market research to help the Government understand the size and demographics of the interested industrial base.) Small Business Size Standard: $45 Million PROJECT OVERVIEW The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Louisville District, has a requirement for the design and construction of Dual Bay (Fuel Cell and General Maintenance) Hangar for the KC-46 Pegasus aircraft at Selfridge ANG, MI. The scope of work consists of furnishing all necessary equipment, materials, labor, supervision, quality control, and supplies to deliver a fully functional maintenance hangar including required shops as indicated below: General Purpose Shop Corrosion Control Shop Fuel Cell Shop: Weapons System Maintenance Engine Shop Avionics Shop Non-Destructive Inspection (NDI) Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: $188,700,000 PLANNED ACQUISITION STRATEGIES UNDER EVALUATION: Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) via Other Transaction Authority (OTA). The Louisville District is evaluating a Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) strategy utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. This authority is intended for military construction projects that involve testing and experimentation associated with new and emergent construction technologies to achieve potential benefits such as enhanced mission resilience, improved installation support, or cost and schedule reduction. Currently, the Government has advanced the design to 35% and has the capability to progress to a full design. Therefore, the Government is utilizing this RFI to assess industry capability, interest, and the advantages of utilizing Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The CM@Risk Course of Action (10 U.S.C. � 2808a): This path allows USACE to execute a construction project where the design is brought at near 65% completion. Phase 1 Preconstruction: The builder is hired during Phase 1 to act as an expert consultant, helping the Designer of Record (DOR) push the design from 65% to 100% using real-time market data and MII (MCACES 2nd Generation) cost comparisons. Phase 2 Construction: Once the design hits 100% and the MII estimate validates the open-book pricing, the agreement transitions to Phase 2, where the builder goes "At-Risk" to construct the facility under a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP). The DOR retains design liability, but the contractor drives constructability and assumes responsibility for layout, schedule, and trade coordination. The CM@Risk Pricing Structure: Preconstruction Services Fee: A small, fixed-price or time-and-materials amount paid to the contractor strictly to fund their time spent helping the Architect Engineer (A/E) finalize the 65% design into a 100% design. The Target Fee: The contractor�s transparent profit margin for managing the actual construction, bid competitively upfront. The GMP: The absolute ceiling for the construction phase (Validated Direct Costs + Target Fee + Shared Contingency). PHASED EXECUTION PLAN Phase 1: Preconstruction Services Agreement (CM@Risk Advisory) Solicitation (White Papers): The Solicitation would likely include the 35% design. The Deliverable is anticipated to be a concise 5-10 page White Paper. Evaluation Criteria will likely include Corporate capability and experience with collaborative project delivery methods ( including CM@Risk, Progressive Design-Build (PDB) and/or Design-Build to Budget (DBtB)) under an OT framework; preconstruction approach (how the firm plans to collaborate with the Government's A/E to close the remaining 65% design gap, identify value-engineering opportunities, and mitigate supply-chain risks); proposed Target Fee (for construction) and Preconstruction Services Fee. The Pitch Meeting (Oral Presentations): A 90-minute pitch where the contractor must bring their Project Manager, Site Superintendent, and their Preconstruction Manager. The Government team assesses how well the contractor's team will integrate with the A/E during the critical final design push. The OT is initially awarded and funded only for the Preconstruction Services Fee. Design Finalization (Bridging the 35% Gap): The contractor�s Preconstruction team sits with the Government and the DOR. Because the design is not locked, they can actively change it. They perform value engineering, finalize equipment selections, and ensure the drawings are 100% constructible. Open Book Pricing vs. MII: As the design reaches 100%, the contractor conducts open-book market outreach. The Government and contractor review actual sub-bids together. USACE cost estimators finalize the Independent Government Estimate (IGE) using the MII software to validate costs and establish the GMP base. Phase 2: Construction Execution Agreement (Going "At-Risk") Execution: The Agreements Officer (AO) executes a bilateral modification to the OT Agreement, incorporating the GMP and funding the physical construction. Risk Allocation: Under CM@Risk, the contractor is now "At-Risk." While the DOR retains design liability, the contractor collaborates to identify constructability conflicts during Phase 1. During Phase 2, while the DOR still owns fundamental engineering failures, the contractor loses the ability to claim "defective design" for constructability issues, material delays, or coordination errors, because they were explicitly paid to help finalize those exact decisions using market and MII data during Phase 1. INFORMATION REQUESTED Interested parties are requested to respond to the following questions to help shape the final acquisition strategy: Company Profile: Q1. Firm Name Q2. Address Q3. Point of Contact (Name, Title) Q4. Phone Number Q5. Email Address Q6. Unique Entity ID Q7. CAGE code Q8. Socioeconomic Status (Other Than Small, Small, 8(a), SDVOSB, etc.) Q9. Participating Role (Prime Contractor, Subcontractor, Design Firm, Other) Other Transaction Authority (OTA) & Statutory Compliance: Q10. Innovative Technologies: The authority for this OTA (10 U.S.C. � 2808a) is focused on prototyping with new or emergent construction technologies. Describe any innovative materials, methods, or technologies your firm could propose for a project of this scale that could lead to cost savings, schedule acceleration, or enhanced facility performance and resilience. Q11. OTA Experience: Describe your firm's previous experience (if any) executing prototype projects under an OTA. Q12. Barriers to Innovation: What commercial or Government-imposed barriers currently make it difficult to propose or implement innovative construction technologies on traditional military construction projects? How could the flexibility of an OTA help overcome these barriers? Q13. Custom Commercial Terms & Dispute Resolution: To optimize the flexibilities of the Other Transaction Authority (OTA) framework, what specific commercial terms (e.g., tailored dispute resolution/rapid escalation mechanisms, commercial milestone payment structures, or shared intellectual property rights for innovative methods) would your firm recommend the Government adopt

title: Link Belt 348 Load Cell, Dardanelle Marine Terminal
description: This notice of Intent to Sole Source is made to satisfy the requirements of Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 5.101.The U.S. Army Corp of Engineers (USACE) Little Rock District (SWL) intens to award a sole-source, Firm-Fixed Priced (FFP) Purchase Order to Lyle Machinery Co (cage 3D6L9). This is a supply purchase order to replace two (2) load cells with calibrations and upper mast pin in sheaves by factory authorized personnel utilizing original equipment manufacturer (OEM). Work will take place at the Dardanelle Marine Terminal. title: Cheshire and Warrington Outline Water Plan
description: The newly established Cheshire and Warrington Combined Authority (CWCA) has recently stated its intention to commission an Independent Economic Review (IER) for the subregion - setting out the evidence for the opportunities for and constraints on local growth. In support of this, it is vital to better understand where water infrastructure may require upgrades to support local ambition, and how we can better work together to ensure that flooding and drought are not impediments to growth whilst ensuring that wider ecosystem services and farming resilience are better supported. Simultaneously, the Water White Paper published in January 2026 committed Government to act on the Independent Water Commission recommendation, setting up Regional Systems Planning in England. DEFRA have set out an intention to pilot this through Regional System Planners (RSPs), established across each region of England with the aim of influencing both PR29 and other water system investment plans. Defra are keen for partnerships to pilot RSP governance and structures during this set-up year. and have set out that they only intend to provide high level direction on form. Within this context there is a significant opportunity to influence water planning, and ensure alignment with local growth and wider environmental ambitions. To support the IER along with engagement with the establishing North West RSP, ECW is seeking to appoint consultants to develop a strategic, place based evidence base and outline water plan that sits between national/regional water planning processes and local spatial, economic, and infrastructure planning.

title: Caerlaverock Cluster-Wildlife and Natterjack Toad Pond Creation
description: We plan to create a mixture of Natterjack Toad ponds (designed to reintroduce historic breeding locations/habitat specifically for this species) (NJT Ponds) and more general habitat and water restoration ponds (HWR Ponds). The HWR ponds are designed to reinstate general habitat, but also to provide natural flood and surface water management, together with diffused pollution control and sediment catchment from adjacent hillside fields â acting as a buffer zone. In winter, the ponds will reach their maximum surface area, providing large waterways for migratory wildfowl. In spring the NJT ponds will reduce in size and leave a small deepening which will heat up quicker to trigger the Natterjack spawn. In summer they will provide habitat for damselflies and aquatic pond insects. We plan to create 24 ponds, totalling approximately 22,000m2 across the estate adding to existing habitat and creating new wetland habitats. 7 will be natterjack toad specific ponds, and 17 general habitat ponds. Rather than thinking of these ponds as individual assets, we have grouped them into pond networks by holding but also layering other wildlife restoration efforts nearby to maximise the ecological benefit for the habitat. The layout of each having been specifically designed to support whole ecosystems.

description: We plan to create a mixture of Natterjack Toad ponds (designed to reintroduce historic breeding locations/habitat specifically for this species) (NJT Ponds) and more general habitat and water restoration ponds (HWR Ponds). The HWR ponds are designed to reinstate general habitat, but also to provide natural flood and surface water management, together with diffused pollution control and sediment catchment from adjacent hillside fields â acting as a buffer zone. In winter, the ponds will reach their maximum surface area, providing large waterways for migratory wildfowl. In spring the NJT ponds will reduce in size and leave a small deepening which will heat up quicker to trigger the Natterjack spawn. In summer they will provide habitat for damselflies and aquatic pond insects. We plan to create 24 ponds, totalling approximately 22,000m2 across the estate adding to existing habitat and creating new wetland habitats. 7 will be natterjack toad specific ponds, and 17 general habitat ponds. Rather than thinking of these ponds as individual assets, we have grouped them into pond networks by holding but also layering other wildlife restoration efforts nearby to maximise the ecological benefit for the habitat. The layout of each having been specifically designed to support whole ecosystems.
